guidance: Compression is the default: answer YES when the arm is moving through free space — reaching, transporting a grasped object, retracting, or broad sweeps. Also answer YES, with real confidence, whenever the gripper is steadily actuating a control that stays FIXED to the scene and is NOT being carried away: pressing a button, flipping a switch, turning a knob, rotating a faucet handle, swinging a spout, or pushing a single door or drawer shut. Closing the fingers AROUND such an anchored control (a knob, faucet handle, spout, switch, or a door/drawer handle you are pushing closed) is steady, non-delicate contact and is YES — it is NOT the grasp moment, because nothing is about to be lifted free. Answer NO only at a genuinely delicate moment: the instant the fingers close to LIFT a free object up off a surface, or while a held object is being threaded, inserted, or precisely aligned into a tight target or receptacle (including hauling a panel open along its hinge/slide). Borderline contact should read as genuinely uncertain — let the threshold decide, do not force NO. Decide from the camera views, not the task name.
